:::: {.hero}
[A reading journey for hands-on practitioners]{.eyebrow}

# Touch is not one sense

::: {.stand}
Skin carries at least two separate systems, and they are not sending the same
message. One tells you *what* you are touching. The other answers mainly to being
touched *affectionately*. It was found by accident, confirmed by a man who had lost the
ordinary sense of touch, and it fires hardest at one particular speed.
:::
::::

This is a reading journey through the research on touch — the
[sense](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Somatosensory_system){.wiki}, not the technique —
in a series of short stops and about half an hour. Every figure can be operated. Every
claim
names its source before you meet it, and says how much that source can carry.

What follows is what we found reading our way through it: what each system responds to,
what touch does to pain and to relationships, and which of the popular claims we could
not get to stand up.

:::: {.about}

::: {.ab}
[Who it is for]{.k}

Anyone whose work involves putting hands on other people: massage therapists,
bodyworkers, physiotherapists, osteopaths, nurses, midwives, somatic and trauma
practitioners. **No science background is assumed** — we did not begin with much
of one either.

Every claim points to a named paper, cited at the top of its section and listed at the
foot of the page it appears on, so you can go and check where we have read it wrong. And
where researchers disagree, which here they do a good deal, we have tried to say so
rather than pick a side.
:::

::: {.ab}
[What is here]{.k}

**[One · the territory](territory.qmd).** Two roads, the receptors they arrive on, and
how finely skin can actually resolve what it feels.

**[Two · the second system](second-system.qmd).** How the slow road was found, the
patient who proved it carries an experience, and the two things it is tuned to.

**[Three · what touch does](what-touch-does.qmd).** Pain, the map of who may touch you
where, and an honest sorting of how sure anyone can be about any of it.

**[Four · being honest about it](being-honest.qmd).** Four things the field has had to
take back, and why the fibre is not the feeling.

**[What we carry back into the room](carry-back.qmd).** What we came away with, where to
go next, and every source in the order the journey met them.
:::

::::

Nothing here is medical advice, and nothing here is a technique manual. It is a record of
what two readers found in the literature, assembled in 2026 from the literature as it
stood — and it cannot tell you what the person in front of you wants.

::: {.hands}
[Before you start]{.t}
If you take one thing from this: **the same touch is not the same experience.** Most of
what follows is the two systems and what each of them answers to — slow, warm, moving
contact on hairy skin. Part four is about why that turns out to be the smaller half.
:::
